GPIO.note: General-purpose digital I/O; peripherals by GPIO function select

levels.when: while IOVDD is powered (5 V tolerance needs IOVDD at 3.3 V)
levels.note: At IOVDD = 3.3 V. Digital IO (FT): fault tolerant, up to 5.5 V with IOVDD at 3.3 V and 3.63 V with it off. VOH and VOL at the selected drive current (2, 4, 8 or 12 mA): iol_ma and ioh_ma are the weakest setting's, since a pin within VOL at 8 mA is within it scaled to 2 mA too

GPIO_ADC.note: GPIO with ADC input; class ANALOG when used as one. ADC reference is ADC_AVDD

levels.note: At IOVDD = 3.3 V. Standard digital IO, not fault tolerant: VIH max IOVDD + 0.3 V (absolute maximum IOVDD + 0.5 V). VOH and VOL at the selected drive current (2, 4, 8 or 12 mA): iol_ma and ioh_ma are the weakest setting's

DVDD.note: Digital core, from the core regulator or an external rail

VREG_AVDD.note: Core regulator analogue supply, RC filtered 33 ohm / 4.7 uF

VREG_LX.note: Core regulator switch node, max 200 mA; block core_reg

VREG_FB.note: Core regulator feedback, taken at COUT; block core_reg

GND.note: Exposed pad; the single external ground connection

RP2350A.note: The package's circuit as the RP2350A reference board fits it (rp2350a_minimal, netlist read by tools/package_circuit.py). Parts by role; `reference_ref` is the board's designator; `near` is the chip pin a decoupling capacitor serves, a placement hint. Nets inside the package by role pin; ports are where it meets the board, named as the board names them. Ground and supply ports must be connected.

ports.note: Pins by number; what each function means, its supply and default net class. SOT-23-5 numbering from Table 3-1; the KiCad symbol Battery_Management:MCP73831-2-OT has the same numbers and names (checked pin by pin).

VDD.note: Charger input (USB VBUS). Operating 3.75-6 V, recommended VREG+0.3 V to 6 V, absolute maximum 7.0 V; bypass to VSS with at least 4.7 uF

VBAT.note: Battery charge output: drain of the internal P-channel pass transistor, to the cell's positive terminal. Regulates to 4.20 V +/-0.75 % (MCP7383X-2); bypass to VSS with at least 4.7 uF

VSS.note: 0 V reference; connect to the battery's negative terminal and the input supply's return

STAT.note: Tri-state charge status: L while preconditioning/fast/CV charging, H at charge complete, Hi-Z in shutdown or with no battery. Sinks up to 25 mA, sources up to 35 mA; VOH is VDD-0.4 V typ, so its high level is the USB supply, not 3.3 V

levels.note: supply is VDD, the charger's input: its high follows the USB supply. VOH is typical, at the sourcing current Table 5-1 gives

PROG.note: Charge current set: RPROG to VSS, IREG(mA) = 1000 V / RPROG(kohm), 2-67 kohm. Floating (or >= 200 kohm, or a logic high) disables the charger

stat.note: L while charging, H at charge complete, Hi-Z in shutdown or with no battery. Its high is VDD (the charger's input, up to 6 V), not a 3.3 V logic level

MCP73831T-2ACI-OT.note: The datasheet's typical application (DS20001984H Figure 6-1, p.17; values from the p.1 figure) as a circuit. Parts by role; the datasheet figure has labels (CIN, COUT, RPROG, RLED, LED), not numbered designators, so `reference_ref` is a conventional designator and each part's note names its figure label. Values are chosen for a 500-1000 mAh 1S cell charged from USB 5 V (see RPROG). D_STAT and R_STAT are the optional status LED: omit both to drop it; STAT is also a signal port.

U1.note: Figure 6-1 'MCP73831/2'. 4.20 V VREG, options AC (p.26). Symbol pins 1 STAT, 2 VSS, 3 VBAT, 4 VDD, 5 PROG match Table 3-1 (p.11) pin by pin.

CIN.note: Figure 6-1 'CIN' (4.7 uF on p.1). VDD needs at least 4.7 uF to VSS (§3.1 p.11). 10 uF 25 V X5R 0805 so that the capacitance left at 5 V DC bias stays above the 4.7 uF minimum (buck.cap.dc_bias_effective); the datasheet itself names only the minimum.

COUT.note: Figure 6-1 'COUT' (4.7 uF on p.1). VBAT needs at least 4.7 uF to VSS for stability with the battery disconnected (§3.2 p.11, §6.1.1.4 p.18). Same part as CIN; at 4.2 V bias it keeps more than 4.7 uF.

RPROG.note: Figure 6-1 'RPROG' (2 kohm on p.1, for 500 mA). IREG = 1000 V / RPROG (§5.1.2 p.15) = 1000 / 4.7 = 213 mA: 0.43C for a 500 mAh cell, 0.21C for 1000 mAh, below the 1C preferred rate (§6.1.1.1 p.17) so one value serves the whole 500-1000 mAh range and the SOT-23-5 dissipates about 0.47 W at 5.0 V in and the 2.79 V fast-charge threshold, not the 1.54 W the datasheet's 500 mA example does (§6.1.1.3 p.18). 1 %: the charger's own IREG spread is +/-10 % (p.3).

R_STAT.note: Figure 6-1 'RLED', 470 ohm on p.1. With a red LED (about 2 V) from 5 V and STAT's 0.4 V typical low (p.4): about 5.5 mA, under STAT's 25 mA sink limit. Optional: omit with D_STAT.

D_STAT.note: Figure 6-1 'LED'. Anode on VDD, cathode through R_STAT to STAT: lit while charging (STAT = L), dark at charge complete (H) and with no input or no battery (Hi-Z), Table 5-1 p.15. Optional: a board omits D_STAT and R_STAT (instance omit) to drop the indicator.

VIN.note: Charger input, the USB 5 V (VBUS). 3.75-6 V operating, 7.0 V absolute maximum (p.3). A hot-pluggable source needs a TVS from VIN to GND at the connector (§6.1.1.2 p.18); that belongs to the board's USB input, not this package.

VBAT.note: The cell's positive terminal (and whatever load the board hangs on the battery). Place the battery connector close to VBAT and VSS (§6.2 p.18).

GND.note: VSS: the cell's negative terminal and the input return (§3.4 p.11).

STAT.note: Charge status for a host, optional: leave it in no_connect if nothing reads it. Tri-state: L charging, H complete, Hi-Z shutdown/no battery (Table 5-1 p.15). Its high is VDD-0.4 V typ (p.4), i.e. about 4.6 V from USB: a 3.3 V host needs a divider, a series resistor into a 5 V-tolerant input, or a level shifter, which this package does not include. With the LED fitted the Hi-Z and H states read alike unless the host adds a pull.

ports.note: Pins by number for the SOT-23-5 (DBV) variant; what each function means and its default net class. The DBV variant has no power-good pin: PG exists only on TLV62569PDDC and TLV62569PDRL (Device Comparison, p.1; Pin Functions, p.3).

VIN.note: Power supply input, 2.5-5.5 V recommended (p.4), 6 V absolute maximum (p.3). Also the high-side switch's drain: CIN goes between this pin and GND.

GND.note: Ground pin: the low-side switch's return and the control ground (one pin, no exposed pad on DBV).

SW.note: Switch node: the internal FETs to the inductor. DC -0.3 V to VIN+0.3 V; -3 V to 9 V for under 10 ns while switching (p.3).

FB.note: Feedback input, regulated to VFB = 0.6 V (0.588-0.612 V). Connect to an external divider from VOUT; 5.5 V absolute maximum.

EN.note: Enable, active high: VIH 1.2 V max, VIL 0.4 V min (2.5 V <= VIN <= 5.5 V). Must not be left floating. Low = shutdown, 0.1 uA typical, 2 uA max.

levels.note: VIH 1.2 V max and VIL 0.4 V min for 2.5 V <= VIN <= 5.5 V; EN's absolute maximum is 6 V, whatever VIN is

source.locator: §5 Pin Configuration and Functions p.3 (DBV top view and Pin Functions table); KiCad Regulator_Switching:TLV62569DBV (extends TLV62568DBV) has the same numbers and names

en.note: Active high, VIH 1.2 V max and VIL 0.4 V min: 1.8 V or 3.3 V logic drives it. Must not float

TLV62569DBV.note: The package's circuit: the datasheet's typical application (Figure 5, p.8; parts Table 3) set for VOUT = 3.3 V from a 1S LiPo (3.0-4.2 V) or USB 5 V (up to 5.5 V), for a battery-powered RP2350A board's 3.3 V rail (up to 600 mA). Parts by role; reference_ref is Figure 5's designator. Nets inside the package by role pin; ports are where it meets the board. Ground and supply ports must be connected; EN is pulled up inside the package.

U1.note: Figure 5 draws the TLV62569P (with PG); the DBV variant has no PG pin (p.1, p.3). The figure gives the IC no designator; U1 is ours.

CIN.note: 10 uF 25 V X5R 0805 (JLC basic). The datasheet's C1 is 4.7 uF 10 V X7R 0805, and 'for most applications, 4.7-uF input capacitance is sufficient; a larger value reduces input voltage ripple' (§8.2.2.5 p.10). 10 uF is margin for DC-bias loss at 4.2-5.5 V; the capacitor maker's bias curve was not read, so how much is left is not quantified.

L1.note: SXN SMNR4020-2.2UH: 2.2 uH +/-20 %, DCR 0.040 ohm +/-30 % (52 mohm max), rated DC current 3.40 A max, 4.0x4.0x2.0 mm, magnetic-resin shielded (smnr4020_ds p.4). 2.2 uH is Table 4's standard value (p.9). Peak current at 600 mA load and VIN = 5.5 V: dIL = 3.3 x (1 - 3.3/5.5) / (2.2u x 1.5 MHz) = 0.40 A, IL,MAX = 0.80 A, so Isat >= 0.96-1.04 A by the 20-30 % margin of §8.2.2.4 p.10; at the IC's full 2 A it is 2.2 A and 2.64-2.86 A, still under 3.40 A, and above the 3 A typical high-side current limit (p.5) only by 0.4 A. The datasheet does not say whether 'rated DC current' is Isat or the heating current; LCSC lists it as Isat. The footprint is KiCad's SWPA4020S land (pads 1.1x3.7 mm at +/-1.5 mm), which covers SXN's recommended 0.95x3.3 mm pads 2.1 mm apart (p.4).

COUT.note: 22 uF 25 V X5R 0805 (JLC basic). Table 4 (p.9) checks 2.2 uH with 10 uF (the standard), 22 uF and 2 x 22 uF for VOUT >= 1.8 V, and anticipates effective capacitance -50 % from tolerance and DC bias. 22 uF rather than 10 uF as margin for DC-bias loss at 3.3 V (the bias curve was not read), and a larger COUT lowers the Power Save Mode overshoot (§7.3.1 p.6). Within the 10-47 uF the device is designed for (§8.2.2.5 p.10).

RFB_TOP.note: VOUT = 0.6 V x (1 + R1/R2) (Equation 2, p.9). For 3.3 V, R1/R2 = 4.5; with R2 = 100k the nearest E96 value is 453k: VOUT = 3.318 V nominal, 3.25-3.39 V over VFB's 0.588-0.612 V (p.4) before resistor tolerance (1 %). Extended part at JLC; 100k/22k basic parts would draw 150 uA instead of 6 uA.

RFB_BOT.note: R2 <= 200 kOhm (§8.2.2.2 p.9); 100 kOhm is the value the feed-forward capacitor recommendation is given for. Divider current 3.3 V / 553 kOhm = 6 uA, against the IC's 35 uA quiescent current (p.4).

CFF.note: Feed-forward capacitor across R1: '6.8-pF capacitance is recommended for R2 of 100-kOhm resistance' (§8.2.2.2 p.9); optional in Table 3 but fitted here for load-transient response (Figure 19 p.12). C0G 50 V. A board that omits it keeps a stable loop (Figure 18 is without it).

R_EN.note: Not in Figure 5, which ties EN straight to VIN. A pull-up to VIN so EN is never floating (§7.4.1 p.7) while the EN port lets a board switch the rail off (a slide switch or open-drain to GND: 4.2 uA through this resistor at a full cell, plus 2 uA max shutdown current, p.4). EN input current is not specified in the datasheet, so 1 MOhm assumes it is well under 1 uA (VIH max is 1.2 V). A board that wants Figure 5 exactly omits R_EN and ties the EN port to VIN. reference_ref R4: the datasheet's R3 is the PG pull-up, absent on DBV.

VIN.note: Input, 2.5-5.5 V (p.4): the battery (3.0-4.2 V) or USB 5 V. Under-voltage lockout at 2.3 V typical, 2.45 V max, falling (p.4).

VOUT.note: 3.3 V output (3.318 V nominal with 453k/100k), up to 600 mA for this board; the IC is rated 2 A (p.4). Follows VIN minus about 84 mV at 600 mA once VIN < 3.40 V (100 % duty cycle, §7.3.2 p.6).

GND.note: Power and control ground: the single GND pin, CIN's and COUT's low sides and the divider's foot.

EN.note: Enable, active high, pulled up to VIN by R_EN. Leave unconnected for always-on, or pull below 0.4 V to shut down (p.4).

ports.note: Pins by number; what each function means, its supply and default net class. LGA-14L numbering from DS12140 Table 1 (pp.7-8) and Figure 3 (p.6). The KiCad symbol Sensor_Motion:LSM6DSM has the same 14 numbers and functions (checked pin by pin); its names differ only in case (SDX, SCX for SDx, SCx).

I2C_SDA.note: I2C/I3C serial data (SDA); SPI SDI / 3-wire SDO when CS is low. No internal pull-up (Table 19 p.38): needs an external pull-up to VDDIO (§5.1.1 p.17). Fast mode, 400 kHz max (Table 6 p.14)

levels.note: supply is VDDIO. VOH and VOL at 4 mA, the pin's maximum drive; control pins take -0.3 V to VDDIO + 0.3 V

I2C_SCL.note: I2C/I3C serial clock (SCL); SPI SPC when CS is low. No internal pull-up; needs an external pull-up to VDDIO

levels.note: supply is VDDIO. VOH and VOL at 4 mA, the pin's maximum drive; control pins take -0.3 V to VDDIO + 0.3 V

SA0.note: I2C address LSb (SA0) in I2C mode, SPI SDO otherwise. Input without pull-up by default (Table 19 p.38): tie to GND (address 0x6A) or VDDIO (0x6B), §5.1.1 p.18

levels.note: supply is VDDIO. VOH and VOL at 4 mA, the pin's maximum drive; control pins take -0.3 V to VDDIO + 0.3 V

CS.note: 1: I2C/I3C enabled (SPI idle); 0: SPI. Tie to VDDIO for I2C (§5.1 p.17). Internal pull-up by default (Table 19 p.38), but the datasheet requires it tied high

levels.note: supply is VDDIO. VOH and VOL at 4 mA, the pin's maximum drive; control pins take -0.3 V to VDDIO + 0.3 V

INT.note: Programmable interrupt outputs, push-pull and active high by default (CTRL3_C PP_OD, H_LACTIVE, p.51). INT1 is an input with pull-down at power-on and must be low or unconnected then if I2C/SPI is used (Table 19 note 2, p.38); INT1 high at power-up selects I3C only (§5.3 p.24). INT2 is driven low by default (Table 19 p.38); INT2 is also DEN

levels.note: supply is VDDIO. VOH and VOL at 4 mA, the pin's maximum drive; control pins take -0.3 V to VDDIO + 0.3 V

AUX_MASTER.note: SDx/SCx: I2C master (Mode 2) or auxiliary SPI (Mode 3/4). In Mode 1 (unused): connect to VDDIO or GND. No pull-up by default

AUX_SPI.note: OCS_Aux / SDO_Aux: auxiliary SPI (Mode 3/4). Unused (Mode 1/2): OCS_Aux left unconnected; SDO_Aux to VDDIO or left unconnected; an unconnected pin is still soldered to its pad (Table 1 note 2, p.8). Both have internal pull-ups by default in Mode 1/2 (Table 19 p.38)

VDD.note: Core supply, 1.71-3.6 V (1.8 V typ); absolute max -0.3 to 4.8 V. 100 nF ceramic as near the pin as possible

VDDIO.note: I/O supply, 1.62-3.6 V; sets the logic levels (VIH 0.7*VDDIO, VIL 0.3*VDDIO) and the pull-up rail. 100 nF ceramic as near the pin as possible

GND.note: 0 V supply, pins 6 and 7; both must be soldered (TN1383 §3.5 p.9)

i2c.note: No internal pull-ups on SDA and SCL: the bus needs them, to VDDIO

spi.note: 4-wire SPI when CS is low: SPC on SCL, SDI on SDA, SDO on SDO/SA0

int1.note: Push-pull and active high by default (open drain or active low by CTRL3_C). Must be low or unconnected at power-up when I2C or SPI is used: high selects I3C only

int2.note: Push-pull and active high by default; driven low at reset. Also the DEN input

aux.note: Sensor hub (Mode 2): an I2C controller for up to four external sensors. Unused (Mode 1): SDx and SCx to VDDIO or GND

LSM6DSOTR.note: The datasheet's Mode 1 connection (DS12140 §7.1 Figure 21, p.35) in I2C mode as a circuit: CS tied to VDDIO for I2C (§5.1 p.17), SDO/SA0 to GND for address 0x6A, SDx/SCx (aux master, unused) to GND, OCS_Aux and SDO_Aux unconnected but soldered (Table 1 notes, p.8), C1/C2 100 nF on VDD and VDDIO, Rpu on SDA and SCL. VDDIO is on the same 3.3 V rail as VDD: the host (RP2350 IOVDD) runs at 3.3 V, so no level shifting is needed and Table 3 (p.12) allows 3.3 V on both; one rail also cannot power VDDIO without VDD. Parts by role; `reference_ref` is the figure's label (C1, C2; the figure's two Rpu are not numbered, so R1/R2 are conventional). R_SDA_PU and R_SCL_PU are optional: a board that has its own pull-ups on the bus omits both (instance omit).

U1.note: KiCad 10 has no LSM6DSO symbol. Sensor_Motion:LSM6DSM matches DS12140 Table 1 (pp.7-8) pin by pin: 1 SDO/SA0, 2 SDx, 3 SCx, 4 INT1, 5 VDDIO, 6 GND, 7 GND, 8 VDD, 9 INT2, 10 OCS_Aux, 11 SDO_Aux, 12 CS, 13 SCL, 14 SDA; only the case of SDX/SCX differs. (LSM6DS3/LSM6DSL were not used: their pins 10 and 11 are NC, where the LSM6DSO has OCS_Aux/SDO_Aux.) Footprint checked against Figure 25 (p.151): pads at 0.5 mm pitch, centres 0.1 mm + half a 0.475 mm pad in from the package edge (x 1.1625, y 0.9125) as in the KiCad pads; KiCad's land is 0.625 x 0.35 mm against TN1383's 0.575 x 0.35 (pad + 0.1 mm), see lsm6dso.land.pattern.

C_VDD.note: Figure 21 'C1 100 nF' on VDD (pin 8): 100 nF ceramic as near as possible to the supply pin (§7.1 p.35; Table 1 note 1 p.8). X7R 16 V 0402.

C_VDDIO.note: Figure 21 'C2 100 nF' on VDDIO (pin 5), placed as near as possible to it (§7.1 p.35). VDDIO shares the 3.3 V rail with VDD but keeps its own capacitor at its own pin, as the figure shows.

R_SDA_PU.note: Figure 21 'Rpu' (10 kohm) from SDA to VDDIO; the lines must have external pull-ups (§5.1.1 p.17). 4.7 kohm instead of ST's 10 kohm so that 400 kHz fast mode meets its 300 ns rise time with up to 300e-9/(0.8473*4700) = 75 pF of bus capacitance (SLVA689A eq. 6, Table 2-1 p.3); 10 kohm allows only 35 pF. Above the minimum (3.3-0.4)/3 mA = 967 ohm (eq. 1). Optional: omit both pull-ups if the board's bus already has them.

R_SCL_PU.note: Figure 21 'Rpu' from SCL to VDDIO; same value and reasoning as R_SDA_PU. Optional with it.

GND.note: Both GND pins (6, 7). SDO/SA0 (pin 1) to GND sets the I2C address LSb to 0: 7-bit address 1101010b = 0x6A (§5.1.1 p.18), leaving 0x6B free for a second LSM6DSx on the same bus; the pin has no pull-up by default (Table 19 p.38), so it must be tied. SDx/SCx (pins 2, 3), the unused I2C-master/aux pins, go to GND as Mode 1 allows ('Connect to VDDIO or GND', Table 1 p.7); GND rather than VDDIO so pins 1-3, side by side, are all on one net with SA0. Route each to the plane with its own trace, not a plane flood onto the pad (lsm6dso.layout.ground_by_trace).

VDD.note: 3.3 V rail for VDD (pin 8, 1.71-3.6 V) and VDDIO (pin 5, 1.62-3.6 V), Table 3 p.12. CS (pin 12) is tied to VDDIO to select I2C (§5.1 p.17). The pull-ups go to VDDIO (§5.1.1 p.17), the same rail.

SDA.note: I2C data to the host; open-drain bus, 400 kHz max (Table 6 p.14).

INT1.note: Interrupt 1 to a host GPIO; push-pull, active high by default (CTRL3_C p.51). Must be low or floating at power-on, or the part comes up I3C-only (Table 19 note 2 p.38, §5.3 p.24): no pull-up on this net, and the host pin must not drive it high before the IMU has booted.

INT2.note: Interrupt 2 (or DEN) to a host GPIO; push-pull, driven low by default (Table 19 p.38). May be left unconnected by a board that does not use it.
